description: real pair with near-identical per-shot rate, largest volume gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the higher-volume player should have >= offensive_value at equal rate
interpretation: PASS is the theoretically required behavior for a total-value metric; a FAIL here would be an implementation bug.

description: real pair with near-identical shot volume, largest per-shot-rate gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the higher-rate player should have >= offensive_value at equal volume

description: real pair tied on scoring_points (24), largest turnover-count gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the player with fewer turnovers should have strictly greater offensive_value
interpretation: Confirms turnover_value strictly discounts scoring credit -- ball security is never free.

description: real pair tied on scoring_points (10), largest points-per-shot gap (i.e. same output, very different volume of attempts to get there)
theoretically_expected_behavior: the more efficient (fewer shots for the same points) player should score higher on offensive_value, since fewer shots means a smaller expected-points baseline to clear
interpretation: Confirms the baseline scales with attempts, not just makes -- taking more shots to reach the same score is priced as below-average efficiency.

description: real pair tied on one_point_goals (5), largest two-point-attempt-share gap
theoretically_expected_behavior: no directional prediction -- selection is a descriptive tendency, not a value claim (model_spec_v1 explicitly does not price selection independently of its shots)
observed_behavior: selection shares differ (0.00 vs 0.44) while offensive_value (2.50 vs 4.11) is driven by shooting_value_raw, not selection share
interpretation: NOT A PASS/FAIL TEST. Confirms (by construction) that two_point_attempt_share_raw does not itself enter offensive_value -- it is a reported descriptive column, exactly as specified.

description: real pair with near-identical win%, largest draw-count gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the higher-volume player should have >= faceoff_value_total (this is the workload confound, expected and disclosed, not a defect)
interpretation: PASS reproduces the mechanical workload effect Phase 10/12 already documented (probe P5).

description: real pair with near-identical draw count, largest win% gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the higher-win% player should have strictly greater faceoff_value_total

description: every above-baseline vs every below-baseline faceoff player
theoretically_expected_behavior: every above-baseline player's value should exceed every below-baseline player's, AT THE SAME VOLUME -- but volume differs, so this need not hold exactly
observed_behavior: min above-baseline value (4.71) vs max below-baseline value (2.12)
interpretation: A FAIL here is expected and is NOT evidence of a defect if it occurs -- it would simply mean a low-volume above-baseline player is outscored in TOTAL value by a high-volume below-baseline one, exactly the workload confound this model discloses rather than corrects.

description: real pair with near-identical save%, largest shots-faced gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the busier goalie should have >= goalie_value_total (the workload confound, expected)
interpretation: PASS reproduces the mechanical workload effect Phase 10/12 already documented (probe P4).

description: real pair with near-identical shots faced, largest save% gap available
theoretically_expected_behavior: the higher-save% goalie should have strictly greater goalie_value_total

description: best-save% small-sample goalie vs best-save% large-sample goalie
theoretically_expected_behavior: no single correct ranking is implied by the model's own definition -- a small-sample goalie's PER-SHOT rate value could exceed a large-sample goalie's, but this table ranks by TOTAL value, which rewards the large sample's cumulative production
observed_behavior: small-sample goalie (11 SOG, save% 0.700): 2.07; large-sample goalie (234 SOG, save% 0.590): 12.51
interpretation: NOT A PASS/FAIL TEST -- the qualification_state column (SMALL_SAMPLE vs QUALIFIED) is exactly how this model discloses which of the two is more trustworthy, rather than resolving the ranking.
